description: Oracle constructs the assessor looks for, with the PostgreSQL / Azure equivalent, a class, and a weight in Ora2Pg-style cost units (5 minutes each, 84 per person-day).

classes.CLEAN: Mechanical. A converter handles it and a reviewer skims it.
classes.PARTIAL: Converts, but behaviour or performance can drift in an edge case. A human checks each use.
classes.REVIEW: A design decision or a hand rewrite on any PostgreSQL target.
classes.BLOCKER: No supported equivalent on Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server. Needs a redesign, an external service, or a different target.

entries.name: CONNECT BY hierarchical query
entries.postgres: WITH RECURSIVE; LEVEL, path and root columns are carried by hand
entries.why: The basic shape converts mechanically. The pseudo-columns and loop detection do not.

entries.name: CONNECT BY pseudo-columns, NOCYCLE, ORDER SIBLINGS
entries.postgres: Carry path, root and depth through the recursive term; add CYCLE (PG 14+) or a visited-path guard
entries.why: Oracle detects cycles with NOCYCLE. PostgreSQL recurses until it runs out of memory unless the query guards itself.

entries.name: ROWNUM
entries.postgres: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (...) or LIMIT, never both interchangeably
entries.why: ROWNUM is assigned before ORDER BY. A naive LIMIT conversion returns a different set of rows.

entries.name: Oracle (+) outer join
entries.postgres: ANSI LEFT/RIGHT JOIN
entries.why: Mechanical for two tables. Predicates on the outer side move between ON and WHERE and change the result.

entries.name: MERGE INTO
entries.postgres: MERGE (PG 15+) or INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE
entries.why: Syntax survives on PG 15+. Concurrency behaviour under load differs and needs a test.

entries.name: MERGE with DELETE WHERE
entries.postgres: WHEN MATCHED AND <cond> THEN DELETE (PG 15+)
entries.why: The conditional DELETE inside the UPDATE branch has a different shape in PostgreSQL.

entries.name: FROM DUAL
entries.postgres: Drop the FROM clause (or use orafce dual)

entries.name: NVL / NVL2 / DECODE
entries.postgres: COALESCE / CASE; orafce supplies nvl, nvl2 and decode
entries.why: DECODE treats NULL = NULL as a match and CASE does not. A converter that emits plain CASE changes results.

entries.name: DECODE with a NULL search value
entries.postgres: CASE WHEN x IS NULL THEN ... END. DECODE treats two NULLs as equal; a simple CASE x WHEN NULL never matches. Whether the orafce decode() keeps the Oracle behaviour is not verified
entries.why: A converter that emits a simple CASE silently changes the result for NULL input.

entries.name: MINUS
entries.postgres: EXCEPT

entries.name: LISTAGG
entries.postgres: string_agg(expr, sep ORDER BY ...)
entries.why: ON OVERFLOW TRUNCATE has no equivalent. WITHIN GROUP ordering moves into the aggregate.

entries.name: KEEP (DENSE_RANK), RATIO_TO_REPORT, NTH_VALUE FROM LAST
entries.postgres: FIRST_VALUE/LAST_VALUE with a frame; x / SUM(x) OVER (); a reversed ORDER BY
entries.why: Ordinary window functions carry over unchanged. These three are Oracle-only spellings.

entries.name: PIVOT / UNPIVOT
entries.postgres: FILTER aggregates, crosstab() from tablefunc, or LATERAL VALUES
entries.why: PostgreSQL has no PIVOT keyword. The column list must be static or the query becomes dynamic SQL.

entries.name: MODEL clause
entries.postgres: None. Rewrite as recursive CTE, window functions or PL/pgSQL
entries.why: Spreadsheet-style MODEL queries have no PostgreSQL counterpart.

entries.name: Flashback query / versions / table
entries.postgres: No AS OF. Point-in-time restore is a server operation that creates a new server. Row history needs history tables (temporal_tables is on the allow-list) or audit triggers
entries.why: An application that reads past data through AS OF needs a data-model change, not a conversion.

entries.name: WITH FUNCTION (inline PL/SQL in SQL)
entries.postgres: Create a real function
entries.why: PostgreSQL cannot declare a function inside a query.

entries.name: Optimizer hints
entries.postgres: Ignored by PostgreSQL. pg_hint_plan is available if a plan must be forced
entries.why: Hints are comments to PostgreSQL. The plans they forced are gone, so the queries need performance testing.

entries.name: FOR UPDATE WAIT n
entries.postgres: NOWAIT or SKIP LOCKED, with lock_timeout for a bounded wait

entries.name: SAMPLE clause
entries.postgres: TABLESAMPLE BERNOULLI | SYSTEM

entries.name: RETURNING ... BULK COLLECT INTO
entries.postgres: RETURNING into an array via a CTE, or a loop

entries.name: DML error logging (LOG ERRORS INTO)
entries.postgres: None. Row-by-row loop with an EXCEPTION block
entries.why: One failing row aborts the whole statement in PostgreSQL.

entries.name: APPROX_* aggregates
entries.postgres: Exact aggregates, or the hll extension for distinct counts

entries.name: CROSS / OUTER APPLY
entries.postgres: LATERAL

entries.name: ROWID / UROWID
entries.postgres: A primary key. ctid is not stable across updates or VACUUM FULL
entries.why: Code that updates or deletes by ROWID needs a real key.

entries.name: ORA_ROWSCN
entries.postgres: xmin as an approximation, or an explicit version column

entries.name: sequence.NEXTVAL / CURRVAL
entries.postgres: nextval('seq') / currval('seq')

entries.name: PRAGMA AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION
entries.postgres: dblink self-connection, or move the write outside the transaction. dblink must be allow-listed on the target
entries.why: Audit rows now roll back with the change they describe, which is a behaviour change someone has to sign off.

entries.name: Other PRAGMAs
entries.postgres: Drop

entries.name: PRAGMA EXCEPTION_INIT
entries.postgres: Catch by SQLSTATE; map ORA- numbers to SQLSTATE values by hand
entries.why: ORA-nnnnn codes do not exist. Each handler needs the matching SQLSTATE.

entries.name: Compound trigger
entries.postgres: Statement-level and row-level trigger pair sharing state through a temp table or transition tables
entries.why: The mutating-table problem it solves does not exist in PostgreSQL, so the right answer is usually a simpler design.

entries.name: Database / schema level triggers
entries.postgres: login_hook for logon logic, event triggers for DDL (an event trigger blocks in-place major version upgrade until dropped)
entries.why: The two halves map to different PostgreSQL mechanisms, and neither behaves exactly like an Oracle system trigger.

entries.name: Trigger ordering (FOLLOWS / PRECEDES)
entries.postgres: PostgreSQL fires same-event triggers in name order

entries.name: :NEW / :OLD correlation names
entries.postgres: NEW / OLD without the colon

entries.name: Row triggers (must RETURN NEW)
entries.postgres: BEFORE ROW trigger functions must end with RETURN NEW
entries.why: A BEFORE ROW function that falls off the end returns NULL and PostgreSQL silently drops the row.

entries.name: INSTEAD OF trigger
entries.postgres: INSTEAD OF row triggers on views are supported

entries.name: BULK COLLECT
entries.postgres: Set-based SQL, or arrays with unnest
entries.why: Row-at-a-time overhead does not exist in PL/pgSQL, so most of these collapse into one statement.

entries.name: FORALL
entries.postgres: A single set-based statement

entries.name: SAVE EXCEPTIONS / SQL%BULK_EXCEPTIONS
entries.postgres: Per-row loop with a BEGIN ... EXCEPTION block
entries.why: Oracle continues past failing rows. PostgreSQL aborts the statement, so a quarantine pattern becomes a slower loop.

entries.name: REF CURSOR / SYS_REFCURSOR
entries.postgres: RETURNS TABLE / SETOF, or REFCURSOR inside one transaction
entries.why: Client drivers handle refcursors badly. The idiomatic fix changes the signature and every caller.

entries.name: Cursor attributes (%ISOPEN, %ROWCOUNT, %FOUND)
entries.postgres: FOUND, GET DIAGNOSTICS ... = ROW_COUNT, or a cursor-open check by name

entries.name: EXECUTE IMMEDIATE
entries.postgres: EXECUTE ... USING with format(%I, %L)
entries.why: Bind placeholders change from :1 to $1 and identifier concatenation must move to quote_ident or format.

entries.name: DDL inside dynamic SQL
entries.postgres: EXECUTE of the DDL, inside the caller transaction
entries.why: Oracle commits either side of DDL. PostgreSQL does not, so the converted routine can deadlock where the original could not.

entries.name: DBMS_SQL
entries.postgres: EXECUTE and format(). orafce provides a subset of DBMS_SQL, so check each call against it

entries.name: Collection types (IS TABLE OF)
entries.postgres: Arrays of scalars or composites, or a child table
entries.why: The mapping is a design decision, not a translation.

entries.name: Associative arrays (INDEX BY)
entries.postgres: jsonb, hstore, or a temporary table
entries.why: PL/pgSQL has no sparse or string-keyed array.

entries.name: VARRAY
entries.postgres: A native array. Add a CHECK for the declared maximum length

entries.name: MULTISET operators
entries.postgres: Array operators, unnest and set operations

entries.name: TABLE() unnest of a collection
entries.postgres: unnest(array) or a set-returning function

entries.name: RECORD types
entries.postgres: A composite type, or the RECORD pseudo-type for a local variable

entries.name: Collection methods (.EXTEND, .LIMIT, .TRIM)
entries.postgres: Array assignment and array_length

entries.name: Pipelined table functions
entries.postgres: RETURNS SETOF with RETURN NEXT / RETURN QUERY
entries.why: Rows are no longer streamed to the caller as they are produced.

entries.name: GOTO
entries.postgres: None. Restructure with loops and EXIT/CONTINUE

entries.name: Overloaded package and type routines
entries.postgres: PostgreSQL overloads functions natively
entries.why: Overload resolution differs. Oracle picks by implicit conversion rank, PostgreSQL raises "function is not unique" for NUMBER versus VARCHAR2 pairs and an untyped literal. Expect explicit casts at call sites.

entries.name: COMMIT / ROLLBACK / SAVEPOINT inside routines
entries.postgres: Allowed in procedures called outside an explicit transaction. Not allowed in functions
entries.why: A function that commits has to become a procedure, and so do its callers.

entries.name: SELECT INTO with NO_DATA_FOUND / TOO_MANY_ROWS
entries.postgres: SELECT ... INTO STRICT
entries.why: Without STRICT, PostgreSQL neither raises NO_DATA_FOUND nor TOO_MANY_ROWS. The handler silently never runs.

entries.name: RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR
entries.postgres: RAISE EXCEPTION ... USING ERRCODE = ...; map -20000..-20999 to custom SQLSTATE values
entries.why: Callers that parse ORA-20nnn from the error text need the same contract.

entries.name: SQLCODE / SQLERRM
entries.postgres: SQLSTATE and SQLERRM

entries.name: User-defined exceptions
entries.postgres: RAISE EXCEPTION USING ERRCODE with a custom SQLSTATE

entries.name: Predefined exception names
entries.postgres: Condition names differ (unique_violation, invalid_text_representation, ...)

entries.name: Error stack and backtrace
entries.postgres: GET STACKED DIAGNOSTICS ... PG_EXCEPTION_CONTEXT

entries.name: DETERMINISTIC
entries.postgres: IMMUTABLE, but only if the function really is
entries.why: Oracle trusts the promise. PostgreSQL uses it to build expression indexes, and a wrong IMMUTABLE corrupts them quietly.

entries.name: RESULT_CACHE
entries.postgres: None. Cache in the application or a table
entries.why: Functions that were cheap because of the cache may not be.

entries.name: PARALLEL_ENABLE
entries.postgres: PARALLEL SAFE

entries.name: AUTHID
entries.postgres: SECURITY INVOKER / SECURITY DEFINER
entries.why: Oracle defaults to definer rights. PostgreSQL defaults to invoker rights, so an unmarked routine changes who it runs as.

entries.name: Object types (AS OBJECT)
entries.postgres: Composite type plus standalone functions
entries.why: Composite types carry no methods, no MAP/ORDER semantics and no substitutability.

entries.name: Object type inheritance (UNDER / NOT FINAL)
entries.postgres: None. Flatten into one composite plus a discriminator

entries.name: MEMBER / STATIC / MAP / ORDER methods
entries.postgres: Standalone functions taking the composite as first argument

entries.name: Package-level session state
entries.postgres: Session GUCs (set_config / current_setting), the session_variable extension (on the allow-list, and a blocker for in-place major version upgrade), a temp table, or a redesign
entries.why: PostgreSQL has no package state. Values that persisted for a session either disappear or move into settings.

entries.name: PLS_INTEGER / SIMPLE_INTEGER / BINARY_INTEGER
entries.postgres: integer
entries.why: SIMPLE_INTEGER wraps on overflow instead of raising.

entries.name: BINARY_DOUBLE / BINARY_FLOAT
entries.postgres: double precision / real

entries.name: ALTER SESSION
entries.postgres: SET / set_config(); NLS_* settings have no equivalent
entries.why: NLS parameters change formatting and sort order and do not exist in PostgreSQL.

entries.name: ANYDATA / ANYTYPE
entries.postgres: jsonb, or the polymorphic pseudo-types anyelement

entries.name: DBMS_ packages (not individually catalogued)
entries.postgres: No generic equivalent. Check orafce, otherwise redesign

entries.name: DBMS_OUTPUT
entries.postgres: RAISE NOTICE; orafce dbms_output for compatible buffering
entries.why: Output is no longer collected by the client unless it reads notices.

entries.name: DBMS_ASSERT
entries.postgres: orafce provides dbms_assert; or quote_ident / quote_literal

entries.name: DBMS_LOB
entries.postgres: text/bytea functions, or the lo_* large-object API

entries.name: DBMS_RANDOM
entries.postgres: random(); orafce dbms_random

entries.name: DBMS_UTILITY
entries.postgres: orafce covers part of the package

entries.name: DBMS_SCHEDULER / DBMS_JOB
entries.postgres: pg_cron on flexible server, or Azure Automation / Logic Apps / Functions for anything beyond a schedule
entries.why: Chains, windows, job classes and event-based jobs have no pg_cron equivalent.

entries.name: DBMS_CRYPTO / DBMS_OBFUSCATION_TOOLKIT
entries.postgres: pgcrypto
entries.why: Algorithm, padding and key handling differ. Existing ciphertext must decrypt under the new calls.

entries.name: Advanced Queuing
entries.postgres: None in the database. Azure Service Bus, or a queue table with SKIP LOCKED
entries.why: Queues have to be re-platformed. Producers and consumers change with them.

entries.name: DBMS_PIPE / DBMS_ALERT
entries.postgres: LISTEN/NOTIFY; orafce provides compatible packages

entries.name: DBMS_LOCK
entries.postgres: pg_sleep(), advisory locks

entries.name: DBMS_APPLICATION_INFO
entries.postgres: SET application_name / set_config('application_name', ...)

entries.name: DBMS_SESSION
entries.postgres: set_config / current_setting

entries.name: DBMS_METADATA
entries.postgres: pg_get_*def functions, pg_dump --schema-only

entries.name: DBMS_STATS
entries.postgres: ANALYZE and autovacuum settings

entries.name: DBMS_MVIEW / DBMS_REFRESH
entries.postgres: REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW [CONCURRENTLY] from pg_cron

entries.name: DBMS_PARALLEL_EXECUTE
entries.postgres: Parallel batches driven from the application or pg_cron

entries.name: DBMS_REDEFINITION
entries.postgres: pg_repack, or logical-replication-based table rewrite

entries.name: DBMS_XMLGEN / XMLDOM / XMLPARSER
entries.postgres: query_to_xml, xmlelement, xpath()

entries.name: UTL_FILE
entries.postgres: orafce emulates UTL_FILE against the server file system, which a managed service does not expose. azure_storage reads and writes blobs; otherwise move the file work to the application tier
entries.why: Every directory object and every path the code writes to needs a new home.

entries.name: UTL_HTTP / UTL_TCP / UTL_SMTP / UTL_MAIL
entries.postgres: No outbound network from the database on flexible server. Azure Functions, Logic Apps or the application tier
entries.why: Database-initiated HTTP and mail calls have to leave the database.

entries.name: UTL_RAW / UTL_ENCODE / UTL_I18N / UTL_COMPRESS
entries.postgres: bytea functions, encode()/decode(), convert_to()

entries.name: PL/SQL web toolkit and APEX
entries.postgres: None. These render pages from the database; the page tier has to be rebuilt
entries.why: Oracle APEX and mod_plsql applications do not run on PostgreSQL.

entries.name: Oracle Text (CONTAINS, CTX_, CTXSYS)
entries.postgres: tsvector full-text search, pg_trgm
entries.why: Ranking and stemming differ, so search results differ.

entries.name: Oracle Spatial (SDO_, MDSYS)
entries.postgres: PostGIS
entries.why: Geometry types map. Spatial operators and index hints do not.

entries.name: Oracle Spatial network / topology / georaster
entries.postgres: pgRouting for networks. No topology/georaster equivalent on flexible server

entries.name: Java stored procedures
entries.postgres: None on flexible server. Move the logic to the application tier
entries.why: There is no in-database Java runtime.

entries.name: External procedures (C libraries)
entries.postgres: None. Untrusted C code is not allowed on a managed service

entries.name: Edition-based redefinition
entries.postgres: None. Use blue/green deployment and expand-contract migrations

entries.name: Streams / Change Data Capture / Advanced Replication
entries.postgres: Logical replication; capture from Oracle needs a product from outside Microsoft

entries.name: Oracle Multimedia
entries.postgres: None. Store media in Blob Storage and metadata in tables

entries.name: Oracle E-Business Suite / Applications packages
entries.postgres: None. A packaged application that requires Oracle Database cannot be moved by moving the database
entries.why: Calls into FND_* mean the schema belongs to a vendor application that is only supported on Oracle.

entries.name: NUMBER without precision
entries.postgres: numeric, or a sized integer type once the real range is known
entries.why: numeric is exact but slower than integer and float. Unconstrained NUMBER hides the range the data actually uses.

entries.name: NUMBER(p) / NUMBER(p,0)
entries.postgres: smallint / integer / bigint by precision

entries.name: NUMBER(p,s)
entries.postgres: numeric(p,s). Negative scale needs PG 15+

entries.name: DATE (carries a time)
entries.postgres: timestamp(0). PostgreSQL date has no time part
entries.why: Mapping to date silently truncates the time of day.

entries.name: VARCHAR2(n BYTE)
entries.postgres: varchar(n), which counts characters
entries.why: Byte-length limits become character limits, so values Oracle rejected are now accepted.

entries.name: NCHAR / NVARCHAR2 / NCLOB
entries.postgres: char / varchar / text in a UTF8 database

entries.name: CLOB
entries.postgres: text
entries.why: Large values slow the load and the comparison.

entries.name: BLOB / RAW / LONG RAW
entries.postgres: bytea (or Blob Storage for large files)

entries.name: LONG
entries.postgres: text
entries.why: LONG columns cannot be read by most change-capture tools and need a special path for the initial load.

entries.name: BFILE
entries.postgres: A path or URL column pointing at Blob Storage
entries.why: The file lives outside the database.

entries.name: XMLTYPE and XML functions
entries.postgres: xml type; xpath(), xmltable() (XPath 1.0 only)
entries.why: XQuery and schema-based XML are not supported.

entries.name: Schema-based XML / XML DB repository
entries.postgres: None. Validate XML in the application tier

entries.name: JSON functions and conditions
entries.postgres: jsonb with SQL/JSON functions (PG 17+ for JSON_TABLE, JSON_QUERY, JSON_VALUE, JSON_EXISTS)
entries.why: Path syntax and error behaviour differ between Oracle and PostgreSQL.

entries.name: INTERVAL YEAR TO MONTH / DAY TO SECOND
entries.postgres: interval
entries.why: PostgreSQL has one interval type, so the two Oracle families lose their separation.

entries.name: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
entries.postgres: timestamptz stores UTC and drops the original offset
entries.why: Oracle keeps the offset that was entered. PostgreSQL does not, so the original zone cannot be read back.

entries.name: TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE
entries.postgres: timestamptz, with the session TimeZone set the way the application expects

entries.name: Time-zone functions
entries.postgres: AT TIME ZONE, current_setting('TimeZone')

entries.name: SYSDATE / SYSTIMESTAMP
entries.postgres: orafce sysdate(), or LOCALTIMESTAMP(0) / clock_timestamp()
entries.why: now() is the transaction start time. SYSDATE is the statement time.

entries.name: ADD_MONTHS / LAST_DAY / NEXT_DAY / MONTHS_BETWEEN
entries.postgres: orafce provides all four

entries.name: TRUNC / ROUND on dates or numbers
entries.postgres: date_trunc() for dates, trunc() for numbers. The type decides

entries.name: TO_CHAR / TO_DATE / TO_TIMESTAMP / TO_NUMBER
entries.postgres: to_char / to_date / to_timestamp / to_number; orafce supplies Oracle behaviour for some
entries.why: pg_catalog sits ahead of orafce on the search path, so the PostgreSQL function wins unless the call is qualified. Format masks differ at the edges.

entries.name: Special date formats ('J', 'SSSSS', 'RRRR')
entries.postgres: to_date with an equivalent mask, or extract(epoch ...)

entries.name: REGEXP_* functions
entries.postgres: regexp_match(es), regexp_replace, ~ operators
entries.why: POSIX flavours differ: character classes, lazy quantifiers and flags.

entries.name: NLS_* functions and settings
entries.postgres: ICU collations, to_char with explicit masks
entries.why: Linguistic sort and case-insensitive comparison change query results and index usage.

entries.name: String concatenation (||) with NULL
entries.postgres: concat() or COALESCE around nullable operands
entries.why: Oracle treats NULL as '' in ||. PostgreSQL returns NULL for the whole expression.

entries.name: Empty string literal ('' is NULL in Oracle)
entries.postgres: Decide per column whether empty and NULL are the same, and rewrite the predicates
entries.why: Nothing fails. Rows quietly move to the other side of IS NULL.

entries.name: IS NULL test on a string
entries.postgres: Decide whether '' and NULL are the same here, and test for both: x IS NULL OR x = ''
entries.why: Oracle stores the empty string as NULL, so an IS NULL test also catches ''. In PostgreSQL it does not, and rows quietly move to the other side of the test.

entries.name: TRIM / TRANSLATE / NULLIF result tested with IS NULL
entries.postgres: TRIM of a blank string is '' in PostgreSQL, not NULL. Test the length or compare to ''
entries.why: The classic 'is it numeric' idiom TRANSLATE(x, ...) IS NULL relies on an empty result being NULL. Converted mechanically it rejects or accepts the wrong rows.

entries.name: Column typed with a VARRAY
entries.postgres: A native array. Add a CHECK for the declared maximum length
entries.why: The declared maximum length is not enforced by an unbounded array.

entries.name: Column typed with an object type
entries.postgres: A composite type column, or flatten the attributes into columns
entries.why: Methods, MAP/ORDER semantics and substitutability do not carry over with the column.

entries.name: SUBSTR / INSTR / LENGTHB family
entries.postgres: substr / strpos / octet_length; orafce supplies instr
entries.why: SUBSTR(s, 0, n) treats 0 as 1 in Oracle and not in PostgreSQL.

entries.name: ROWID / UROWID columns
entries.postgres: text or a real key

entries.name: SYS_GUID
entries.postgres: gen_random_uuid() (uuid, not RAW(16))
entries.why: The value type changes from RAW(16) to uuid and sort order changes with it.

entries.name: ORA_HASH / STANDARD_HASH
entries.postgres: md5(), sha256() from pgcrypto
entries.why: Hash values differ. Anything persisted or compared across systems breaks.

entries.name: CAST (MULTISET ...)
entries.postgres: array_agg

entries.name: Range / list / hash partitioning
entries.postgres: Declarative partitioning. The primary key must include the partition key
entries.why: A unique key that omits the partition key is refused, and every foreign key to it follows.

entries.name: Interval partitioning
entries.postgres: pg_partman creates future partitions on a schedule
entries.why: PostgreSQL does not create partitions on demand.

entries.name: INTERVAL clause
entries.postgres: See DDL-PARTITION-INTERVAL

entries.name: Composite partitioning
entries.postgres: Multi-level partitioning, declared by hand

entries.name: Reference / system / virtual-column partitioning
entries.postgres: None. Redesign the partition key onto the table itself

entries.name: Global index on a partitioned table
entries.postgres: No global indexes. A unique or primary key on a partitioned table must include the partition key, which changes the data model. Local indexes per partition, or a different key

entries.name: Index-organized table
entries.postgres: A heap table plus CLUSTER on the primary key index
entries.why: The physical ordering is not maintained after writes.

entries.name: External table
entries.postgres: azure_storage reads blobs. file_fdw is not available on a managed service

entries.name: Global temporary table
entries.postgres: CREATE TEMP TABLE per session, or UNLOGGED
entries.why: The definition is permanent in Oracle and per-session in PostgreSQL, so every session has to create it.

entries.name: NESTED TABLE ... STORE AS
entries.postgres: A child table

entries.name: Virtual / generated column
entries.postgres: GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) STORED, or VIRTUAL on PG 18+
entries.why: The expression must be immutable and the column now takes space.

entries.name: Identity column
entries.postgres: GENERATED ... AS IDENTITY

entries.name: DEFAULT ON NULL
entries.postgres: A BEFORE INSERT trigger, or COALESCE in the writer

entries.name: Invisible columns / indexes
entries.postgres: None for columns. Drop the index or use a view

entries.name: Table / index compression
entries.postgres: Dropped. TOAST compresses large values. Size the target without it
entries.why: Hybrid Columnar Compression ratios do not carry over, so the data is larger on the target.

entries.name: Physical storage clauses
entries.postgres: Dropped. Tune fillfactor where the table is write-heavy

entries.name: LOB storage clause
entries.postgres: Dropped

entries.name: CHECK constraint
entries.postgres: CHECK

entries.name: DEFERRABLE constraint
entries.postgres: DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED

entries.name: NOVALIDATE / DISABLE constraint
entries.postgres: NOT VALID for foreign keys and checks only. A disabled constraint has no equivalent
entries.why: Existing violations in legacy data block the constraint.

entries.name: ON DELETE SET NULL / CASCADE
entries.postgres: Same syntax

entries.name: Bitmap index
entries.postgres: btree, GIN or BRIN. PostgreSQL builds bitmaps at query time
entries.why: The access pattern that justified the bitmap index needs a different index design.

entries.name: Function-based index
entries.postgres: Expression index. The function must be IMMUTABLE

entries.name: Reverse key index
entries.postgres: Hash index, or no index

entries.name: Domain / text index
entries.postgres: GIN or GiST

entries.name: Materialized view fast refresh / ON COMMIT
entries.postgres: REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW [CONCURRENTLY] on a schedule. Core PostgreSQL has no incremental refresh. pg_ivm (on the allow-list) maintains simple views incrementally and needs a test per view
entries.why: Freshness guarantees change. ON COMMIT views are stale until the next refresh.

entries.name: Query rewrite
entries.postgres: None. Queries must name the materialized view
entries.why: Queries that were transparently accelerated slow down.

entries.name: Materialized view log
entries.postgres: Dropped with the fast-refresh design
entries.why: Logs exist only to support fast refresh.

entries.name: Remote objects through a database link
entries.postgres: oracle_fdw (on the flexible server allow-list, PG 12-18) reaches a remote Oracle, postgres_fdw reaches PostgreSQL. Both need a network path from the server to the remote system
entries.why: A foreign table is not a database link: no distributed transactions, different pushdown, and every remote object needs its own foreign table.

entries.name: CREATE DATABASE LINK
entries.postgres: A foreign server plus user mapping (oracle_fdw)

entries.name: Synonym
entries.postgres: A view, or an entry on search_path

entries.name: WITH READ ONLY / FORCE view
entries.postgres: REVOKE write privileges. A view cannot be created before its dependencies exist

entries.name: Sequence ORDER / NOCACHE / CYCLE / SCALE
entries.postgres: CACHE 1, CYCLE. ORDER and SCALE have no equivalent
entries.why: PostgreSQL sequence caches are per session and gaps are normal, so gap-free numbering needs a different design.

entries.name: Sequence KEEP / GLOBAL
entries.postgres: Informational

entries.name: Virtual Private Database (DBMS_RLS)
entries.postgres: CREATE POLICY row level security
entries.why: The policy function becomes a USING expression. Policies that depend on session context need that context set first.

entries.name: DBMS_RLS call
entries.postgres: CREATE POLICY row level security

entries.name: Fine-grained auditing
entries.postgres: pgaudit object auditing

entries.name: SYS_CONTEXT('USERENV', ...) / USERENV()
entries.postgres: session_user, current_user, current_setting('application_name'), inet_client_addr()
entries.why: Most USERENV keys have a direct PostgreSQL function. A few (for example CLIENT_IDENTIFIER) have to be set by the application.

entries.name: SYS_CONTEXT on an application context / CREATE CONTEXT
entries.postgres: current_setting('app.key') and set_config(); the writer of the context becomes an explicit call
entries.why: Oracle restricts who may write an application context to its trusted package. A custom setting can be written by anyone, so the guarantee has to be rebuilt.

entries.name: Application context object
entries.postgres: A custom GUC namespace

entries.name: Column encryption
entries.postgres: pgcrypto or application-level encryption. Storage is encrypted by the service

entries.name: Database Vault / Label Security / Data Redaction
entries.postgres: None. Redesign with row level security, views and roles

entries.name: Profiles, users, roles
entries.postgres: Roles. Password policy moves to Entra ID or the platform
entries.why: Authentication moves to Microsoft Entra ID in most Azure estates.

entries.name: Data dictionary and V$ views
entries.postgres: pg_catalog and information_schema, pg_stat_*
entries.why: Catalog queries return different columns, so each one is rewritten.

entries.name: SQL*Loader / external utilities
entries.postgres: COPY, pg_dump / pg_restore, azure_storage

entries.name: TIMESTAMP(n) with n > 6 (nanoseconds)
entries.postgres: timestamp(6) - PostgreSQL stores microseconds; digits 7-9 are rounded away.

entries.name: VARCHAR2 / NVARCHAR2 with BYTE or CHAR semantics
entries.postgres: varchar(n) or text. PG counts CHARACTERS, never bytes, so a byte-sized Oracle limit becomes looser (no overflow). orafce varchar2 keeps byte semantics, nvarchar2 character semantics.

entries.name: CHAR(n) / NCHAR(n) blank-padded
entries.postgres: char(n) (bpchar) keeps padding semantics but comparisons against text/varchar strip trailing blanks differently than Oracle; usually safer as varchar(n) + CHECK(length = n) or fixed text, after reviewing joins.

entries.name: Oracle BOOLEAN (PL/SQL, 23ai SQL) and Y/N flag idiom
entries.postgres: boolean. For NUMBER(1)/CHAR(1) Y/N flag columns decide whether to convert (Ora2Pg REPLACE_AS_BOOLEAN); callers comparing to 'Y'/1 must change.

entries.name: SUBTYPE declarations
entries.postgres: CREATE DOMAIN (schema level) or substitute the base type; PL/pgSQL has no package-local subtypes.

entries.name: %TYPE / %ROWTYPE anchors
entries.postgres: Native: table.col%TYPE and table%ROWTYPE are valid PL/pgSQL. Cursor %ROWTYPE works for named cursors; %ROWTYPE of a package-local record type does not.

entries.name: Identifier longer than 63 bytes
entries.postgres: PG truncates identifiers to 63 bytes (NAMEDATALEN-1) - rename and watch collisions; Oracle 12.2+ allows 128 bytes.

entries.name: PG-reserved words used as column/attribute names
entries.postgres: Quote or rename (Ora2Pg adds 12 units = one hour per reserved-word table/column). Words reserved in PG but legal in Oracle: limit, offset, window, analyse, binary, both, leading, trailing, placing, returning, similar, symmetric, variadic, verbose, lateral...

entries.name: Quoted identifiers containing lower-case (mixed-case names)
entries.postgres: Decide: rename to snake_case (recommended) or keep quoted mixed case and quote it everywhere (every unquoted reference then fails). Same applies to quoted aliases in views consumed by apps.

entries.name: NLS session/sort/format settings and NLSSORT()
entries.postgres: No NLS layer: use ICU collations (CREATE COLLATION), lc_numeric/DateStyle/TimeZone GUCs and explicit to_char/to_date formats. orafce offers oracle.nlssort()/oracle.set_nls_sort() and the orafce.nls_date_format GUC as partial emulation.

entries.name: Case/accent-insensitive comparison (BINARY_CI, LINGUISTIC)
entries.postgres: citext (allowlisted) for case-insensitive columns, or a nondeterministic ICU collation (CREATE COLLATION ... deterministic = false). Nondeterministic collations: LIKE is supported from PG18 only; PK/FK columns must share a collation.

entries.name: SELECT INTO / NO_DATA_FOUND / TOO_MANY_ROWS
entries.postgres: PL/pgSQL SELECT INTO silently yields NULL on zero rows and takes the first row on many unless written SELECT ... INTO STRICT, which raises no_data_found / too_many_rows. Add STRICT wherever the Oracle code relies on the exceptions (or on their absence).

entries.name: FOR loop REVERSE
entries.postgres: PL/SQL counts down from the SECOND bound to the first; PL/pgSQL counts down from the FIRST to the second - swap the bounds.

entries.name: Implicit cursor FOR loop variable (FOR r IN (SELECT ...))
entries.postgres: Declare the loop variable (record) explicitly in DECLARE.

entries.name: ORDER BY inside a derived table with ROWNUM (top-N-after-sort idiom)
entries.weightOrigin: ora2pg-25.0:ORDER BY inside a derived tabl
entries.postgres: LIMIT n with ORDER BY (the wrapped form is the correct translation); the unwrapped WHERE ROWNUM <= n ... ORDER BY form returns arbitrary rows in Oracle and must NOT become ORDER BY ... LIMIT.

entries.name: INSERT ALL / INSERT FIRST (multi-table insert)
entries.postgres: Several INSERT statements, or one statement with data-modifying CTEs (WITH i1 AS (INSERT ... RETURNING), i2 AS (INSERT ...)). INSERT FIRST needs mutually exclusive WHERE predicates.

entries.name: IGNORE NULLS / RESPECT NULLS in analytic functions
entries.postgres: NOT available in PG 18 (the newest version on Azure flexible server): emulate with a LATERAL/subquery on the last non-null row, or array_agg(x) FILTER (WHERE x IS NOT NULL). PostgreSQL 19 (beta 4, not GA) adds IGNORE NULLS/RESPECT NULLS.

entries.name: FETCH FIRST / OFFSET (12c row limiting)
entries.postgres: Supported as written (FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY / WITH TIES from PG13). FETCH FIRST n PERCENT ROWS has no equivalent.

entries.name: WITH FUNCTION / WITH PROCEDURE (12c inline PL/SQL)
entries.postgres: No inline functions: create a (temporary) function or inline the expression.

entries.name: FOR UPDATE NOWAIT / SKIP LOCKED
entries.postgres: Supported as written in PG. Throughput under contention differs; test queue-style consumers.

entries.name: UPDATE/DELETE/INSERT through an inline view (key-preserved join)
entries.postgres: UPDATE ... FROM joined_table or MERGE; PG cannot update an inline view.

entries.name: RETURNING ... INTO / BULK COLLECT INTO on DML
entries.postgres: PL/pgSQL supports RETURNING ... INTO var (use STRICT for single-row). RETURNING ... BULK COLLECT INTO has no analogue: use CTE + array_agg or a loop.

entries.name: ROLLUP / CUBE / GROUPING SETS / GROUPING_ID / GROUP_ID
entries.postgres: ROLLUP, CUBE, GROUPING SETS and GROUPING() exist; GROUPING_ID(a,b) -> GROUPING(a,b); GROUP_ID() has no equivalent.

entries.name: Views: FORCE / WITH READ ONLY / editioning
entries.postgres: FORCE views (invalid at creation) do not exist: create dependencies first. WITH READ ONLY -> REVOKE write privileges (no view-level read-only flag). WITH CHECK OPTION is supported.

entries.name: SOUNDEX / UTL_MATCH
entries.postgres: fuzzystrmatch: soundex(), difference(), levenshtein(); UTL_MATCH.EDIT_DISTANCE -> levenshtein.

entries.name: Join/DML syntax: UPDATE ... SET (a,b) = (SELECT ...)
entries.postgres: Supported (multi-column assignment from a subquery) - verify cardinality (single row).

entries.name: WHEN OTHERS THEN
entries.postgres: Supported, but OTHERS does not catch QUERY_CANCELED or ASSERT_FAILURE, and every block with an EXCEPTION clause opens a subtransaction (expensive; also forbids COMMIT inside). Ora2Pg charges 10 units per WHEN OTHERS because it hides bugs.

entries.name: Collection methods (.COUNT .FIRST .LAST .NEXT .PRIOR .EXISTS .EXTEND .TRIM .DELETE .LIMIT)
entries.postgres: array_length(arr,1), array_lower/upper, array_append/array_cat, arr[i], = ANY(arr), arr = arr[1:n]; DELETE/EXISTS on sparse collections need a different structure.

entries.name: Cursor expressions CURSOR(SELECT ...) / nested cursors
entries.postgres: No equivalent: return arrays of rows (ARRAY(SELECT ROW(..))) or json_agg, or split into several queries.

entries.name: INSERTING / UPDATING / DELETING predicates
entries.postgres: TG_OP = 'INSERT' / 'UPDATE' / 'DELETE'; UPDATING('col') -> NEW.col IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.col.

entries.name: Trigger REFERENCING (row correlation renames)
entries.postgres: PG REFERENCING only declares transition TABLE names (NEW TABLE AS / OLD TABLE AS); renaming the row variables is not supported - use NEW/OLD in the function body.

entries.name: Conditional compilation ($IF / $$PLSQL_*)
entries.postgres: No preprocessor: resolve at conversion time (keep the active branch) or turn into ordinary IF on a configuration function.

entries.name: Wrapped PL/SQL (obfuscated source)
entries.postgres: Cannot be converted: obtain the original unwrapped source first. Until then the unit is a blocker (converter emits a placeholder that raises an error).

entries.name: Mutating-table workarounds (ORA-04091)
entries.postgres: PG has no mutating-table restriction (row triggers may read/modify the table; AFTER triggers see the final state), so statement-level collectors, autonomous-transaction hacks and compound triggers written to dodge ORA-04091 can usually be deleted and re-expressed as plain AFTER triggers or set-based logic - but each needs a behaviour review.

entries.name: Sequence bounds beyond bigint (default MAXVALUE 28 digits) and SCALE/EXTEND/SESSION (18c)
entries.postgres: PG sequences are bigint (max 9223372036854775807): cap MAXVALUE; SCALE/EXTEND (scalable sequences), SESSION sequences and KEEP have no equivalent.

entries.name: Identity columns / sequence defaults
entries.postgres: GENERATED {ALWAYS|BY DEFAULT} AS IDENTITY (PG10+). ON NULL (insert NULL -> generate) has no equivalent: use BEFORE trigger/COALESCE. Explicit-value INSERT behaviour differs between ALWAYS and BY DEFAULT in PG (OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE).

entries.name: Invisible columns (12c)
entries.postgres: No invisible-column attribute: expose through a view that omits the column or REVOKE column privileges; SELECT * and INSERT-without-column-list behaviour changes (the column now appears).

entries.name: Database links and @link references
entries.postgres: Foreign data wrapper per link target: oracle_fdw (Azure allowlisted, GA Dec 2024, PG12-18) to keep reading Oracle during transition; postgres_fdw/dblink for PG; tds_fdw for SQL Server/Sybase. Credentials/TNS do not translate; remote procedure calls (proc@link) and DML with distributed 2PC have no FDW equivalent.

entries.name: Materialized view (complete/on-demand refresh)
entries.postgres: MATERIALIZED VIEW + REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW [CONCURRENTLY] (needs a unique index, still a full recompute). Schedule refreshes with pg_cron; PG has no refresh groups.

entries.name: Private temporary tables (18c)
entries.postgres: CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE ... ON COMMIT DROP | PRESERVE ROWS.

entries.name: Partition maintenance and partition-extended syntax
entries.postgres: EXCHANGE -> DETACH/ATTACH PARTITION; ADD/DROP -> CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION OF / DROP TABLE; TRUNCATE partition -> TRUNCATE the child; SELECT ... PARTITION(p) -> select from the child table; SPLIT/MERGE PARTITIONS have no PG18 syntax (manual copy); PG19 betas added ALTER TABLE ... SPLIT/MERGE PARTITIONS and Beta 4 reverted them.

entries.name: Physical storage clauses on indexes/tables (to drop)
entries.postgres: Drop (PCTFREE can become fillfactor = 100 - PCTFREE). Oracle tablespace/storage tuning has no PG counterpart on a managed service.

entries.name: NOVALIDATE / ENABLE / DISABLE / RELY constraint states
entries.postgres: NOT VALID (+ later VALIDATE CONSTRAINT) works for FOREIGN KEY, CHECK and (PG18) NOT NULL only; UNIQUE/PK cannot be NOT VALID; DISABLE/RELY have no equivalent (drop the constraint, or disable the trigger for load windows).

entries.name: USING INDEX clause on PK/UNIQUE
entries.postgres: PRIMARY KEY (...) INCLUDE (...) / USING INDEX TABLESPACE dropped; to reuse an existing index: ADD CONSTRAINT ... PRIMARY KEY USING INDEX name.

entries.name: Tablespaces and datafiles
entries.postgres: Remove TABLESPACE clauses and CREATE TABLESPACE; storage is managed by the service (default tablespace only).

entries.name: Clusters and hash clusters
entries.postgres: Recreate as plain or partitioned tables (Ora2Pg cost 0 = not supported). PG CLUSTER is only a one-off reorder.

entries.name: Immutable / blockchain tables, NO DROP/NO DELETE
entries.postgres: No equivalent: enforce with triggers that reject UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE, REVOKE privileges, and an external hash chain if tamper evidence is required.

entries.name: Oracle Sharding
entries.postgres: No single-database equivalent. Redesign the distribution strategy; Azure flexible server offers elastic clusters (GA per release notes, Nov 2025) as a horizontally distributed option - suitability must be assessed per workload.

entries.name: Hybrid partitioned tables (external partitions)
entries.postgres: Converts as an ordinary table; external partitions are lost - load that data separately (azure_storage / COPY).

entries.name: Views with Oracle-specific options (VIEW ... OF type, WITH OBJECT IDENTIFIER, constraint on view)
entries.postgres: Object views and view-level (disabled) constraints have no equivalent: use plain views; keep constraints as documentation comments.

entries.name: LOCAL (partitioned) index keyword
entries.postgres: Drop LOCAL: a PG index created on a partitioned table is automatically partitioned alongside the table (one index per partition).

entries.name: Data redaction (DBMS_REDACT)
entries.postgres: Masking views / column privileges / application masking, or the PostgreSQL Anonymizer extension (anon 2.5.1 on PG13-18, 1.3.2 on PG11-12; needs shared_preload_libraries).

entries.name: Auditing: DBMS_FGA / AUDIT statements / unified audit policies
entries.postgres: pgaudit (allowlisted: 18.0 on PG18, 16.0 on PG16-17, 1.7 on PG15; needs shared_preload_libraries) for session/object audit logged to Azure logs; row-condition fine-grained auditing and handler modules -> triggers writing an audit table. Audit settings are server parameters on Azure.

entries.name: GRANT / REVOKE (object and system privileges)
entries.postgres: Recreate from the source inventory. System privileges (CREATE ANY TABLE, SELECT ANY TABLE, ...) have no equivalent - map to schema-level grants + ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES; PG grants EXECUTE on functions to PUBLIC by default; Oracle has no per-column UPDATE-only semantics identical to PG.

entries.name: Schema-level privileges (23ai: GRANT ... ON SCHEMA)
entries.postgres: GRANT ... ON ALL TABLES/SEQUENCES/FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA + ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES (covers future objects); GRANT ... ON SCHEMA in PG grants USAGE/CREATE on the schema itself, not its contents.

entries.name: JSON_VALUE / JSON_QUERY / JSON_EXISTS / JSON_TABLE
entries.postgres: Available from PG17 (JSON_TABLE, JSON_QUERY, JSON_VALUE, JSON_EXISTS); on PG16 or older use jsonb operators and jsonb_path_query. Default ON ERROR/ON EMPTY behaviour and RETURNING type must be checked.

entries.name: In-Memory column store (INMEMORY)
entries.postgres: No columnar in-memory store: rely on shared_buffers/OS cache, pg_prewarm (allowlisted), covering indexes, summary tables or read replicas for analytics.

entries.name: Data Pump / RMAN / exp-imp / file transfer
entries.postgres: pg_dump/pg_restore from a client, Azure automatic backups and point-in-time restore, geo-redundant backup options; scripted refresh/clone jobs need rewriting.

entries.name: LogMiner / GoldenGate / Streams / CDC packages
entries.postgres: Logical decoding: wal2json and pglogical are allowlisted (preload required) for CDC; native logical replication for PG-to-PG; Debezium-style connectors run outside the database.

entries.name: OLAP option, analytic views, data mining
entries.postgres: No PostgreSQL target: rebuild as views/materialised summary tables (OLAP) or move model scoring to Azure ML / the application (data mining).

entries.name: SQL macros (SQL_MACRO) and polymorphic table functions
entries.postgres: Simple SQL-language functions are inlined by the PG planner (closest to scalar macros); table macros/PTFs need set-returning functions or views.

entries.name: SQL domains (23ai CREATE DOMAIN)
entries.postgres: PG CREATE DOMAIN covers single-column base type + DEFAULT + CHECK/NOT NULL; Oracle multi-column, flexible and enum domains, DISPLAY/ORDER expressions, annotations and JSON-schema domains need CHECKs, enum types or functions.

entries.name: Schema annotations (23ai ANNOTATIONS)
entries.postgres: No annotations: store as COMMENT ON ... or a metadata table; no dictionary views.

entries.name: SQL property graph / GRAPH_TABLE / SQL/PGQ (23ai)
entries.postgres: Not in PostgreSQL 18. SQL/PGQ was committed for PG19 (2026-03-16) and then REVERTED on 2026-09-07; PG19 Beta 4 (2026-09-24) does not contain it, and nothing is committed for PG20 yet. Options on Azure: Apache AGE (openCypher; allowlisted 1.7.0 on PG17-18) or WITH RECURSIVE + adjacency tables; queries and DDL must be rewritten.

entries.name: Vector data type and search (23ai/26ai AI Vector Search)
entries.postgres: pgvector (vector 0.8.2: vector/halfvec/bit/sparsevec types, HNSW and IVFFlat) and pg_diskann (0.6.5, PG14-18) for disk-based ANN; VECTOR_DISTANCE(a,b,COSINE) -> a <=> b, EUCLIDEAN -> <->, DOT -> <#> (negated); FETCH APPROX FIRST n -> ORDER BY ... LIMIT n using the ANN index; embeddings via azure_ai (2.0.0 on PG18) instead of DBMS_VECTOR.

entries.name: JSON Relational Duality Views
entries.postgres: No equivalent (updatable JSON documents with ETag concurrency over normalised tables, REST/GraphQL). Rebuild as views + INSTEAD OF triggers + jsonb aggregation, or an API/ORM layer in the application.

entries.name: JavaScript stored procedures (MLE)
entries.postgres: plv8 (allowlisted 3.2.4, trusted) can host JavaScript logic; MLE module/env/import semantics, JSON/SQL driver APIs and npm-style modules differ. Often simpler to rewrite in PL/pgSQL.

entries.name: Lock-free reservations (RESERVABLE columns)
entries.postgres: No equivalent: atomic UPDATE ... SET qty = qty - n WHERE qty >= n (CHECK constraint) or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED patterns.

entries.name: IF [NOT] EXISTS / GROUP BY ALL / alias / FROM-less SELECT (23ai SQL conveniences)
entries.postgres: IF [NOT] EXISTS and SELECT without FROM are supported by PG; GROUP BY alias/position is supported; GROUP BY ALL is not (expand the columns).

entries.name: Select AI / DBMS_CLOUD_AI / DBMS_CLOUD
entries.postgres: azure_ai extension (allowlisted; Azure OpenAI embeddings/completions, Azure AI Language/Translator calls from SQL) for AI calls; DBMS_CLOUD object-store calls -> azure_storage or the application.

entries.name: Native BOOLEAN in SQL (23ai) / BOOLEAN columns
entries.postgres: boolean (same literals TRUE/FALSE/NULL; PG also accepts yes/no/on/off/1/0 strings).

entries.name: DBMS_SCHEDULER jobs that run OS executables or scripts
entries.postgres: There is no operating system to run a program on. Move the job to Azure Automation, Azure Functions, a container job or a VM, and call the database from there.
entries.why: pg_cron runs SQL inside the server and nothing else.
